children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning an assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me gather some information about your child or children to assess your eligibility.

**First, I need to know about your child's age:**

How old is your child (or the youngest child if you have more than one)?
- Are they **under 16**?
- Are they **16 to 19**?
- Are they **20 or over**?

This will help me determine which eligibility requirements apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 13 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 13 years old, they fall into the **under 16 category**, which means Alex would automatically qualify as a child for Child Benefit purposes.

Now let me continue with the next eligibility check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

Since Alex is 13, they're likely not in full-time work, but I want to confirm this to ensure there are no issues.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're just in school like any other 13-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what we need. Since Alex doesn't work at all, they meet this requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about any benefits Alex might be receiving:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?** Specifically, is Alex not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

(For a 13-year-old in school, this would be unlikely, but I need to confirm)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just a regular kid.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

For a 13-year-old, this is very unlikely, but I need to confirm:
- Is Alex NOT in any apprenticeship?
- Or are they in an approved apprenticeship (specifically a Foundation Apprenticeship in Wales)?
- Or are they in a disqualifying apprenticeship?

I'm guessing Alex is simply not in any apprenticeship at all, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex isn't in any apprenticeship. They're only 13, so they're just in regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is just in regular school and not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation, as this is an important eligibility requirement for Child Benefit. There are several possible paths that could make you eligible - let me check which applies to you:

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - this is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **You have pre-settled status and are working** (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. **You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work** (jobseeker, up to 91 days)
5. **You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources** and not claiming certain means-tested benefits
6. **You have pre-settled status and are studying** with sufficient resources
7. **You have pre-settled status as a family member** of an EEA or Swiss national
8. **You are a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which of these, if any, describes your situation? Or do you simply normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you're living abroad, let me ask a few more questions to determine if you still meet the residency requirements:

**Can you tell me which of the following applies to your situation?**

1. **Are you a Crown servant?** (e.g., working for the UK government, diplomatic service, military, etc.) - and if so, are you living in certain qualifying countries?

2. **Do you have any EU Settlement Scheme status?** (either settled status or pre-settled status) - perhaps from living in an EU country previously?

3. **Is there any other special circumstance** that might apply to your situation?

Or alternatively, do you have any ongoing connection to the UK - such as normally living there when not abroad, or planning to return soon? This would help me understand your residency status better.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant, and I don't have any EU Settlement Scheme status. I just live abroad - no special circumstances or connection to the UK in terms of residency.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Based on what you've told me, it appears you don't meet any of the residency pathways that would qualify you for Child Benefit. The residency requirement is a fundamental eligibility criterion, and since you:

- Don't normally live in the UK
- Don't have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Don't have pre-settled status
- Are not a Crown servant living abroad in qualifying countries
- Have no other special circumstances

Let me navigate to confirm this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to deliver this news, but based on the eligibility rules for Child Benefit, **you are not eligible** for the following reason:

**Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Reason:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**What this means:**
Child Benefit requires that the person claiming must normally live in the UK, or meet one of several special circumstances (such as having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, being a Crown servant living abroad in certain countries, or other qualifying criteria). Since you currently live abroad without any of these qualifying circumstances, you don't meet this fundamental eligibility requirement.

**Next Steps:**
- If your situation changes in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK or your residency status changes - you could reapply
- If you believe you might have qualifying status (such as EU Settlement Scheme status) that you didn't mention, you could explore that further with HMRC
- For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I understand this may be disappointing news. If you have any questions about this decision or believe your circumstances might be different, feel free to contact HMRC directly for further guidance.

Now let me record this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've recorded the assessment outcome. Unfortunately, despite Alex meeting all the criteria related to their age and circumstances as a child, your claim for Child Benefit cannot be approved because of the residency requirement.

If you have any further questions or if your situation changes, please don't hesitate to ask or contact HMRC directly.

reasonings: Alex is 13 years old (under 16), does not work, does not receive benefits in their own right, and is not in any apprenticeship. However, the claimant does not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant currently lives abroad without settled status, pre-settled status, Crown servant status, or any other qualifying circumstances that would allow them to claim Child Benefit for Alex despite residing outside the UK.
arguments.overall_reasoning: While Alex meets all the child-specific eligibility criteria (being under 16, in school, with no disqualifying factors), the claim is ineligible because the claimant does not meet the residency requirements. Child Benefit requires the claimant to normally live in the UK or meet special residency circumstances, none of which apply in this case."
